extracted.intended_audience: readers of the edited volume (scholars/general readers) and distributors/users of Project Gutenberg eBooks
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and practical choices for selecting, arranging, and lightly editing personal letters for publication (biographical volume), together with Project Gutenberg redistribution/licensing requirements for electronic distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criterion: illustrate personal character
rubrics_metrics.description: In choosing letters for publication I have been largely guided by the wish to illustrate my father's personal character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select letters primarily for their ability to illuminate the subject's personal character rather than for completeness; favor letters that illuminate manner of working and traits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrange chapters to follow author's career and major works
rubrics_metrics.description: The chief part of the book falls into chapters whose titles correspond to the names of his books.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize material so that chapters map to the subject's major projects/books, allowing the life narrative to follow intellectual/work development rather than strict life chronology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chronological order where practicable, but prioritize coherence by subject
rubrics_metrics.description: I have adhered as far as possible to chronological sequence, but the character and variety of his researches make a strictly chronological order an impossibility ... a rigidly chronological series of letters would present a patchwork of subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use chronological sequencing as a guideline, but group letters thematically or by subject when chronology would fragment coherent narratives; indicate approach in Table of Contents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicate omissions/insertions (usual plan)
rubrics_metrics.description: In printing the letters I have followed (except in a few cases) the usual plan of indicating the existence of omissions or insertions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mark omissions and editorial insertions in letters to preserve documentary transparency, except in exceptional cases explained in notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissive silent insertion of small function words to smooth text
rubrics_metrics.description: My father's letters give frequent evidence of having been written when he was tired or hurried, and they bear the marks of this circumstance. In writing to a friend, or to one of his family, he frequently omitted the articles: these have been inserted without the usual indications, except in a few instances, where it is of special interest to preserve intact the hurried character of the letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For small omitted words (e.g., articles) that are clearly lapses from haste, editors may insert them silently to improve readability except where the omission itself is of interest and should be preserved and indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bracket insertion for other small words
rubrics_metrics.description: Other small words, such as 'of', 'to', etc., have been inserted usually within brackets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use brackets to indicate editorial insertions of small words beyond articles, maintaining a record of emendations while aiding comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial normalization of spelling, capitals, and punctuation
rubrics_metrics.description: I have not followed the originals as regards the spelling of names, the use of capitals, or in the matter of punctuation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normalize orthography, capitalization, and punctuation for readability and consistency, but note that originals were not strictly followed; keep record of major deviations in apparatus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not over-emphasize original underlining with italics
rubrics_metrics.description: My father underlined many words in his letters; these have not always been given in italics,--a rendering which would unfairly exaggerate their effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Render original emphases (underlines) judiciously—avoid wholesale conversion to italics which might distort emphasis density; selectively retain emphasis when significant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use auxiliary sources (diary) to supply dates and framework
rubrics_metrics.description: The Diary or Pocket-book, from which quotations occur in the following pages, has been of value as supplying a frame-work of facts round which letters may be grouped. He rarely dated his letters, so that but for the Diary it would have been all but impossible to unravel the history of his books. It has also enabled me to assign dates to many letters which would otherwise have been shorn of half their value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where primary documents lack dates, use contemporaneous diaries, pocket-books, or other records to assign dates and provide a structural framework; document such assignments in notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit use of received letters when provenance incomplete
rubrics_metrics.description: Of letters addressed to my father I have not made much use. It was his custom to file all letters received, and when his slender stock of files ... he would burn the letters of several years ... This process ... destroyed nearly all letters received before 1862.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious in relying on incoming correspondence when archival completeness or provenance is compromised; explain absences and selection biases transparently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgements policy: credit contributions but not name critics
rubrics_metrics.description: I have received much help from my friends ... To some I am indebted for reminiscences of my father, to others for information, criticisms, and advice. To all these kind coadjutors I gladly acknowledge my indebtedness. The names of some occur in connection with their contributions, but I do not name those to whom I am indebted for criticisms or corrections, because I should wish to bear alone the load of my short-comings, rather than to let any of it fall on those who have done their best to lighten it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge substantive assistance and contributions; withhold naming those who provided private criticisms/corrections when desirable to protect contributors or take editorial responsibility.
